newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-LIPINSKI SHINES AGAIN, CHEN LU FLOPS.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-LIPINSKI SHINES AGAIN, CHEN LU FLOPS.

text.p: Texan Tara Lipinski continued as figure skating's flavour of the month on Monday as former world champion Chen Lu of China flopped in pursuit of a second title.

The tiny, 14-year-old Lipinski continued blissfully along the path that took her to two upset wins over current world champion Michelle Kwan in the past month, winning her qualifying group from team mate Nicole Bobek as Kwan won the other group despite another disappointing display.
But Chen, 20, could not overcome the effects of a long-term foot injury as well as problems at home with the Chinese authorities.

Chen, champion two years ago and runner-up in a splendid shoot-out against Kwan last year, completed only one triple jump, doubled out of another, fell and managed only single jumps in place of four other planned triples.
She placed 11th of 21 in her group from which 15 qualified for the main event on Friday.
A recurrence of a stress fracture that knocked her out of the 1994 world championships in Japan has rendered Chen a mere shadow of her former self.
"She has only been training for three or four weeks," her coach, Zhu Li-ming, said.
"She needed more time for training. She was not ready for this competition but she had to do it to qualify for the Olympics."
Under new rules governing next year's Japan Olympics, a country must place a skater in the top 24 this week to be sure of an entry.
It was crucial that Chen took part as team mate Du Yankun did not qualify for the main event, which will comprise the top 15 skaters from each of the two groups.
Chen's marks for technique dipped as low as 4.2 out of the 6.0 maximum, though her supreme artistry gained her higher scores -- and kept her from an embarrassing elimination.
Lipinski showed no sign of the nerves one might expect from a 14-year-old who placed 15th a year ago but who now has a chance to become the youngest women's champion in history.
"I get a little nervous, everyone does. But I know when to stop being too nervous," she said.

Her programme again included the difficult triple loop-triple loop jump combination she has pioneered and she won a unanimous decision from the flamboyant Bobek with Russian Maria Butyrskaya third in the group.
A month ago Lipinski was merely a contender for a spot on the U.S. team here. Then she became U.S. champion and later won the Champions Series final.
Though Kwan won her group from Vanessa Gusmeroli of France and European champion Irina Slutskaya of Russia, it was again not a vintage performance.

Her opening jump combination of triple lutz-triple toe loop was scaled down to triple-double, she doubled out of a planned triple flip and did only a single axel where she planned a double late in her routine.
"I kind of chickened out of a couple jumps," she said.
"I think I've learned a lesson from the last two events," said Kwan. "I went in saying 'Oh my God, this is a Nationals, Oh my God this is the Champions Series'.
"Now I'm trying to forget what the competition is and just focus on my skating. I'm trying to get my mental edge back and get my head stronger," she said.
Gusmeroli skated a fine routine to circus music but Slutskaya, like Kwan, was disappointing, failing to do what she intended with her first two jumps.
